spec: SPEC-053 / SPEC-004 CON-003 — the Path-B resolver closure
what: The closed schema for one resolver closure, as EVERY stack that recognises one must read it.
why: This schema had four recognisers — the LFE hub shell, the browser module, the Rustler NIF and the WASM facade — and two had already drifted on a security check: assertion methods were compared by value natively and by COUNT in the browser. The DECISION is now shared. The RECOGNISERS cannot be: they sit at trust boundaries in three runtimes, and full recognition must happen at the boundary. Shared vectors are what makes their disagreement fail a test instead of a frame.
authority: selfsame's `PathBClosureFacts` is the producer and its serde field names are the wire. A change here is a change to that type, and every consumer's pinned copy must move with it.
two_wires: TWO wires, and THREE readers. The RESOLVER wire has nine members and is seen only by the browser module, which fetches for itself and so refuses a resolver that supplies `fetched_at_seconds`. Once that module stamps the member, the closure is on the STAMPED wire of ten members -- which is the same shape the sidecar hands the LFE hub shell, and the same shape the WASM facade deserialises. So the browser module reads nine and everything downstream of it reads ten. Neither wire is a superset by accident.
resolver_id_sentinel: Every case carries `resolver_id`: "state-1". A harness MUST substitute the declared resolver identity it is exercising wherever that exact string appears, and MUST leave any other value alone — one reject case sets resolver_id to a NUMBER on purpose, and a harness that overwrote it unconditionally would silently pass that case.

sidecar.note: Ten members, the fetch stamp already applied. Read by the LFE hub shell, by the WASM facade, and by the Rustler NIF. Named for its producer, but it is the shape every reader downstream of a stamp sees.

accept.why: empty lists are legal: a DID with no assertion methods is a fact, not a malformed answer
every boolean at its other value, with populated lists — a recogniser judges shape, never the verdict
a fetch at the epoch is a shape that must pass; whether it is too old is the verifier's decision, not the recogniser's

reject.why: a missing member — the schema is closed, so an absent field is not a defaulted one
an unexpected member; a recogniser that ignores extras lets a producer smuggle state past the others
a boolean spelled as a string — one stack coerces, another refuses, and the check silently passes on one of them
resolver_id as a number: identity is compared as a string, and a coerced one may compare equal by accident
null for a boolean — absent and false are different claims
a 31-byte key: Ed25519 length is a boundary every stack must reject identically
a 33-byte key — secp256k1 SEC1 length, which must not pass as Ed25519
a key as a base64 string: the sole accepted spelling is the number array serde emits for Vec<u8>
a byte of 256 — out of range, and a stack that masks it would accept a different key than the others
a negative byte, for the same reason
an unexpected member inside a nested method — a nested map is a trust boundary too
a missing member inside a nested method
a non-string in the revocation set: ids are compared as strings, so a number would never match and would silently withhold a revocation
a non-string alias, for the same reason
a list member given as a string
null for a list — an empty revocation set and an absent one are different claims
the sidecar wire carries the fetch stamp; without it no freshness bound can be applied at all
the stamp as a string
a fractional stamp — seconds are integers, and a stack that truncates disagrees with one that refuses

resolver.note: Nine members, as a resolver presents one. Read ONLY by the browser module, which stamps the tenth itself.
